stem: A discrete random variable X has the following PMF: P(X=1)=0.15, P(X=2)=0.25, P(X=3)=0.35, P(X=4)=0.25. What is the value of F(3), the cumulative distribution function at X = 3?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.35 is only P(X=3), the PMF value at 3, not the CDF which accumulates all values up to and including 3.
1.00 equals F(4), the CDF at the maximum value; the student applies the cumulative sum all the way to X=4 instead of stopping at X=3.
0.40 arises from summing only P(X=1) + P(X=2) = 0.15 + 0.25 = 0.40, omitting P(X=3) from the accumulation.

explanation: The CDF F(x) = P(X <= x) accumulates all PMF values from the smallest value up to and including x. F(3) = P(X=1) + P(X=2) + P(X=3) = 0.15 + 0.25 + 0.35 = 0.75.

explanation_sections.punchline: CDF is a running total up to and including the argument: F(3) = 0.15 + 0.25 + 0.35 = 0.75.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: discrete CDF from PMF table. Decisive move: F(x) = sum of P(X=k) for all k <= x. Accumulate: F(1)=0.15, F(2)=0.40, F(3)=0.75, F(4)=1.00. Read off F(3).
explanation_sections.lesson: The CDF at point x is a cumulative sum; the PMF at x is a single probability. Do not confuse them.
explanation_sections.timing: 40 seconds. Sum 0.15+0.25+0.35=0.75. Trap: reporting only 0.35 which is just the PMF, not the CDF.
